narrative: Material PL1__MD2C777C shows smooth, high-volume daily demand averaging 1,938 units with a CV of 0.218, consistent with a normal-like distribution and no detectable trend across the observation window. Lead times are variable (CV=0.575, mean 2.23 days), making lead-time variability the dominant driver (94%) of buffer requirements. A continuous-review (s,Q) policy was selected: safety stock of 4,220 units covers the 95th-percentile lead-time demand, while the order quantity of 6,427 (EOQ-derived and capacity-capped) balances holding and ordering costs within the 12,057-unit storage constraint.
warnings: 18 outliers detected and winsorised at [478.6, 2911.5] bounds
Storage capacity cap applied: unconstrained EOQ 6863 reduced to 6427 to satisfy max_storage_units constraint with safety stock
SAP safety stock is 0 — current policy carries significant stockout risk at 95% service level target

research_insights.selected_model: (s, Q) continuous-review reorder-point with fixed order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand regime (CV=0.218) with near-100% non-zero fraction and normal-like distribution makes the classical EOQ-based (s,Q) model optimal. Continuous review is warranted given high daily volume and variable lead times where periodic review would accumulate excess stockout risk.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds the order quantity: the unconstrained EOQ of 6,863 units was reduced to 6,427 to keep safety_stock + order_quantity (10,647) within the 12,057-unit storage limit. This represents a modest 6.3% reduction in order size and slightly increases ordering frequency, with negligible service-level impact.
